The EIN online assistant has a published operating window: "This tool is available during the following times (Eastern Time): Mon–Fri: 6:00 a.m. – 1:00 a.m. (next day); Sat: 6:00 a.m. – 9:00 p.m.; Sun: 6:00 p.m. – 12:00 a.m." — an online filing rail that keeps business hours.
Published daily limit on the EIN online assistant: "You can apply for only 1 EIN per responsible party per day."
Published session constraint on the EIN online assistant: one session, no save — "It expires after 15 minutes of inactivity, and you'll need to start over."

The EIN fallback rail is published with exact coordinates: mail or fax Form SS-4 to "Internal Revenue Service, Attn: EIN Operation, Cincinnati, OH 45999, Fax: 855-641-6935" (for applicants in the 50 states or DC).

Modernized e-File is a system-to-system machine channel: "MeF uses the widely accepted Extensible Markup Language (XML) format." Transmission requires becoming an Authorized IRS e-file Provider — a credentialed rail, not a public API.

The e-file provider enrollment path is published with its clock: "it can take up to 45 days from the date of submission for the IRS to approve your e-file application" — and principals without professional status "need to be fingerprinted using the IRS authorized vendor".

E-file provider suitability includes a physical step for non-credentialed principals: individuals without current professional status "need to be fingerprinted using the IRS authorized vendor" (Livescan).

A genuine machine intake exists for information returns: IRIS "receives information through two intake channels: IRIS Taxpayer Portal/UI and IRIS Application to Application (A2A)" — the A2A channel is gated by a Transmitter Control Code.

IRS online account sign-in requires identity proofing through ID.me: "You'll need an account with ID.me to sign in to access your tax information and use services on IRS.gov." The same page's data-handling note names "selfie, video, and biometric data" — a liveness check, which no agent can complete for a person.

The ID.me verification path is biometric: "All selfie, video, and biometric data are automatically deleted for users who verify for the IRS" — the account wall in front of IRS online services is a liveness check, not credential MFA.

The 83(b) election's paper rail, in the IRS's own words (Pub 525 update): "You can make the choice by filing a written statement, or Form 15620, Section 83(b) Election, with the Internal Revenue Service Center where you file your return."

An online rail now exists for signed forms including Form 15620 (83(b) election), but it ends at the taxpayer personally: "Online Account (OLA) is required to complete mobile friendly forms that require signatures" — and OLA sign-in is the ID.me liveness wall.

The EIN assistant documents a sanctioned delegation rail: a third-party designee may apply, with signed authorization from the responsible party — the published intermediary channel commercial formation services ride.
